text_blocks.snippet: A low FODMAP diet is a short-term dietary approach that restricts specific types of carbohydrates (fermentable oligosaccharides, disaccharides, monosaccharides, and polyols) to help manage digestive symptoms, particularly in individuals with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS). It involves identifying and eliminating high-FODMAP foods that can trigger digestive discomfort, then gradually reintroducing them to pinpoint individual triggers.
snippet_highlighted_words: a short-term dietary approach that restricts specific types of carbohydrates (fermentable oligosaccharides, disaccharides, monosaccharides, and polyols) to help manage digestive symptoms, particularly in individuals with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS)

text_blocks.snippet: FODMAPs are short-chain carbohydrates that are poorly absorbed in the small intestine and can be fermented by bacteria in the large intestine, leading to gas, bloating, and other digestive symptoms.
